text: The same tracks coming back in the opposite direction
why: Paragraph 122 states that Watson saw the same tracks coming back in the opposite direction.

text: Thursday evening, following the double track towards King's Pyland
why: The party is on the moor in the evening (sun sinking, ¶113), on Thursday (¶13), and is following the track toward King's Pyland (¶122).

text: When the double track turned off towards King's Pyland
why: Paragraph 122 states that the double track turned sharp off toward King's Pyland at this point.

text: When the same tracks came back the other way
why: Paragraph 122 states that the same tracks were seen coming back the other way at this point.

text: Why did the man with the horse set off towards King's Pyland and then turn back?
why: A plain question raised directly by the tracks in ¶122, worded without pointing to an answer.

text: Why did the man with the horse set off towards King's Pyland and then turn back? — he meant to return the horse, then decided to keep it
id: q.turned_back=he meant to return the horse, then decided to keep it
why: Nothing so far suggests the man meant to return the horse or changed his mind about keeping it; this specific intent is not yet a reasonable consideration for the reader.

text: Why did the man with the horse set off towards King's Pyland and then turn back? — he went that way for some other reason, such as to keep out of sight
id: q.turned_back=he went that way for some other reason, such as to keep out of sight
why: The police search, the gypsies, and Simpson's arrest give the reader reason to consider that the man avoided being seen, and the label stays general.
